project_specification.project_name: nullius — local per-call LLM token usage and spend tracking
project_specification.addition_summary: On 2026-10-07 the operator asked how much the running smoke campaign had spent and the system could not say: no provider call's token usage is persisted, so spend is only visible in the vendor console. The per-pin BudgetedProvider counts tokens in memory and loses them at exit, and providers.Usage folds cache writes into input_tokens although Anthropic bills cache writes, cache reads and plain input at three different rates. This spec records every authoring call's usage locally, attributes it to campaign, node, role and pin, prices it from a dated price table, and reports it from a command. It adds no dependency: the store uses the standard library's sqlite3 and the costs use decimal. So "how much has this campaign spent?" has an exact local answer.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace / SQLite via DATABASE_URL / pytest.
existing_context.test_baseline: main after bug_spec_sampling_record_contract.xml: gate command (uv run --all-packages pytest -n 4 --dist loadfile) 1648 passed; providers 1447, signal-agent 781, orchestrator 433 (+5 runsc skips).
existing_context.conventions:
Follow CLAUDE.md. House CLI pattern as in orchestrator/dream.py (argparse prog "python -m pkg.mod"; main(argv=None, *, env=None, ...) -> int; exit 0/1/2; one JSON line per row; one stderr line per refusal with a code word; no traceback). A CLI module is never imported eagerly by its package __init__. Tests never reach the network or read a credential and pass under pytest-xdist with tmp stores. A store creates its table with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS on connect, like the ops stores.
Facts the features rely on: - providers.Usage(input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens=0). providers._anthropic sets input_tokens = input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens, and cache_read_tokens = cache_read_input_tokens. Cache-creation tokens are not exposed separately. - providers.AuthoringSession.provider_for(role, *, campaign_id, node_id) answers (provider, pin), each pin wrapped once in a BudgetedProvider with the config's ceilings. signal_agent._llm_author calls it for every root, child and retry authoring call. - A Completion carries .model (the served model) and .usage.

category.name: Usage Capture
category.feature: System reports cache-write tokens separately on every completion, so that an Anthropic answer's usage returns plain input, cache writes, cache reads and output as four distinct counts. - providers.Usage gains cache_write_tokens: int = 0 (non-negative, validated like the others). input_tokens keeps its current meaning (every input token the call consumed), so no existing reader changes. - providers._anthropic sets cache_write_tokens from the response's cache_creation_input_tokens. Other backends leave it 0. - Tests: a recorded Messages response with all three input counters maps to the four fields. An old-shape response without cache counters gives zeros. Existing Usage equality and the budget totals are unchanged.

System prices a call from a dated, versioned price table, so that estimate_cost(model, usage) returns a USD figure or None, never a guessed price. - providers._prices holds PRICE_TABLE_VERSION (a date string) and, per model id, USD per million tokens for plain input, cache write, cache read and output, with its source noted. The 2026-09-25 Anthropic first-party list rates are: - claude-opus-5-5: 4.00 / 5.00 / 0.20 / 20.00 - claude-sonnet-5-5: 2.00 / 2.50 / 0.20 / 10.00 - claude-haiku-4-5: 1.00 / 1.25 / 0.10 / 5.00 Cache write is 1.25 times input for the 5-minute TTL. - estimate_cost(model, usage) prices plain input = input_tokens minus cache_write_tokens minus cache_read_tokens, plus each other class at its rate. It returns a Decimal rounded to 6 places. - A model id the table does not map exactly returns None. That includes a dated served id such as claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, unless the table lists that exact id. The caller records "unpriced", never zero. - Tests check each priced model against hand-computed values, the plain-input subtraction, an unknown model returning None, and that the version string is present.

System saves every provider call's usage to an append-only provider_call_usage table, so that each call returns one stored row with its tokens, attribution and estimated cost. - The table is created on connect. Its columns are: - id, recorded_at (UTC ISO-8601) - campaign_id, node_id (nullable) - role, pin (provider/model/version), served_model - input_tokens, cache_write_tokens, cache_read_tokens, output_tokens - est_cost_usd (TEXT decimal or NULL), price_table_version - outcome (ok | error | refused_budget), duration_ms - UsageRecordingProvider(inner, *, store, campaign_id, node_id, role, pin) is a Provider wrapper. On a completion it records one ok row and returns the completion unchanged. On an exception from the inner provider it records one row with outcome error (or refused_budget for BudgetExhaustedError) and zero tokens, then re-raises the same exception. check_model and every other Provider method pass through. - A store write failure never breaks or alters the call. It is logged once per process as a warning, and the call's result or exception stands. - UsageStore(database_url).resolve(env) returns None without DATABASE_URL. Its reads are rows(campaign_id=None) and totals(group_by=("campaign_id","pin")), which sums tokens and est_cost_usd and counts unpriced rows separately. - Tests cover an ok row with exact counts and cost, the error and refused_budget rows with the exception re-raised unchanged, a failing store leaving the call intact, totals grouping, and an unpriced model counted as unpriced.

System records the usage of every authoring call a campaign makes, so that each provider AuthoringSession.provider_for returns is wrapped in a UsageRecordingProvider bound to that call's campaign_id, node_id, role and pin whenever a usage store is configured. - The session takes an optional usage_store, and the composed authoring path supplies UsageStore.resolve(env), so a deployment with DATABASE_URL records automatically. Without one, behaviour is byte-identical to today. - Recording sits outside the budget wrapper. A call the budget refuses is recorded as refused_budget, and budget totals and ceilings are unchanged. - Tests: a session with a fake resolver and a tmp store authors a root, a child and a retry, and the table holds three rows with the right campaign_id, node_id, role and pin. Without a store, no rows and no behaviour change. A budget refusal records one refused_budget row.

category.name: Usage Reporting
category.feature: System reports spend from `python -m providers.usage [--campaign ID] [--by campaign|pin|role|node]` and displays one JSON line per group plus a total line. - Each group line carries calls, input_tokens, cache_write_tokens, cache_read_tokens, output_tokens, est_cost_usd and unpriced_calls. The total line also names price_table_version. - --campaign latest selects the most recent campaign. No rows prints a total of zero calls and exits 0. No DATABASE_URL exits 2. - run.sh gains a `llm-usage` verb (python -m providers.usage "$@", DATABASE_URL defaulting as the campaign verb does, no op run). It is listed by `./run.sh help`. - Tests cover grouping, --campaign latest, the empty store, the missing DATABASE_URL, and an unpriced row surfacing in unpriced_calls.

project_specification.integration_points: Features 1 and 2 are independent foundations. Feature 3 needs both. Features 4 and 5 read feature 3's store.
project_specification.out_of_scope: Dashboard and API surfaces for spend. Enforcing dollar ceilings (token ceilings already exist). Backfilling usage for calls made before this lands.
